bottom_line: Clopidogrel plus aspirin, as compared with placebo plus aspirin, did not significantly reduce the primary end point (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22).
implications: In this broad high-risk population, the reported primary composite outcome did not differ significantly between clopidogrel plus aspirin vs placebo plus aspirin (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22), while the principal secondary composite outcome was lower (relative risk, 0.92; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.86 to 0.995; P = 0.04) and bleeding was increased for moderate bleeding (relative risk, 1.62; 95 percent confidence interval, 1.27 to 2.08; P<0.001) with a non-significant increase in severe bleeding (P = 0.09).

major_points.text: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in a broad high-risk population; clopidogrel 75 mg daily plus low-dose aspirin vs placebo plus low-dose aspirin; median follow-up 28 months.
major_points.quote: We randomly assigned 15,603 patients with either clinically evident cardiovascular disease or multiple risk factors to receive clopidogrel (75 mg per day) plus low-dose aspirin (75 to 162 mg per day) or placebo plus low-dose aspirin and followed them for a median of 28 months.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy end point was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.
major_points.quote: The primary efficacy end point was a composite of myocardial infarction, stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.

major_points.text: Primary efficacy outcome was not significantly different between groups (6.8% vs 7.3%).
major_points.quote: The rate of the primary efficacy end point was 6.8 percent with clopidogrel plus aspirin and 7.3 percent with placebo plus aspirin (relative risk, 0.93; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.83 to 1.05; P = 0.22).

major_points.text: Principal secondary composite end point was reduced with clopidogrel plus aspirin (16.7% vs 17.9%).
major_points.quote: The respective rate of the principal secondary efficacy end point, which included hospitalizations for ischemic events, was 16.7 percent and 17.9 percent (relative risk, 0.92; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.86 to 0.995; P = 0.04)

major_points.text: Severe bleeding was numerically higher with dual therapy (1.7% vs 1.3%), and moderate bleeding was higher (2.1% vs 1.3%).
major_points.quote: The rate of the primary safety end point (severe bleeding according to the GUSTO definition) was 1.7 percent in the clopidogrel group and 1.3 percent in the placebo group (relative risk, 1.25; 95 percent confidence interval, 0.97 to 1.61; P = 0.09).

inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible to enroll in the trial if they were 45 years of age or older

inclusion_criteria.text: Had multiple atherothrombotic risk factors, documented coronary disease, documented cerebrovascular disease, or documented symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.
inclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were eligible to enroll in the trial if they were 45 years of age or older and had one of the following conditions: multiple atherothrombotic risk factors, documented coronary disease, documented cerebrovascular disease, or documented symptomatic peripheral arterial disease.

exclusion_criteria.text: Taking oral antithrombotic medications or nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs on a long-term basis (cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitors permitted).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were excluded from the trial if they were taking oral antithrombotic medications or nonsteroidal antiinflammatory drugs on a long- term basis (although cyclooxygenase-2 inhibitors were permitted).

exclusion_criteria.text: In the investigator's judgment, had established indications for clopidogrel therapy (e.g., recent acute coronary syndrome).
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients were also excluded if, in the judgment of the investigator, they had es- tablished indications for clopidogrel therapy (such as a recent acute coronary syndrome).

exclusion_criteria.text: Scheduled to undergo revascularization could not enroll until after the procedure; excluded if considered to require clopidogrel after revascularization.
exclusion_criteria.quote: Patients who were scheduled to undergo a revascularization were not allowed to enroll until the procedure had been completed; such patients were excluded if they were considered to require clopidogrel af- ter revascularization.

criticisms.text: P values for subgroup association and interaction were only marginally significant; observation should be interpreted with caution; subgroup analysis was only one of several performed.
criticisms.quote: the P value for this association and the P value for the interaction between enrollment status and therapy were only marginally significant, suggesting that this observation should be interpreted with caution, especially since this subgroup analysis was only one of several such analyses performed.

criticisms.text: Unclear how symptomatic vs asymptomatic classification could be implemented clinically because some asymptomatic patients had a history of symptoms or cardiovascular events.
criticisms.quote: Finally, as a practical matter, it is unclear how such a classification could be implemented clinically, since some patients in the asymptomatic subgroup actually had a history of symptoms or cardiovascular events.
